contradiction: Let N0 be the natural-number cardinality of users mapped by S.types.toType to type 0.
typeWeight casts N0 to a real number without dividing by the population size m. The canonical reduction and its surjectivity wrapper use this weight without normalization.
twoTypeReducedModel alpha v has weight alpha at type 0. Projecting weight 0 from the exact structure equality hred gives (N0 : Real) = alpha.
Surjectivity hTypes gives a user of type 0, hence N0 >= 1. The premise halpha1 gives alpha < 1. Thus 1 <= alpha < 1, a contradiction.
Already hred, hTypes and halpha1 are inconsistent. Independently, hred with 0 < alpha < 1 forces a natural-number cast strictly between 0 and 1. The primed premises have the same defect.
The formal implication is vacuously true; no claim is made that its inequality is false or that the paper theorem is false.
